Case: Yang is a 44-year-old who presents with 2 months of low-back and leg pain. The pain started after a day of heavy yard work and has progressed gradually over time. In the last three weeks, he endorses tripping and stumbling more frequently, and has been told by friends that he is dragging his left foot. At present time he is most concerned about the increasing severity of pain, which is affecting his ability to function. When you examine Yang, you confirm that he has a left foot drop with diminished sensation in the sole of his foot. You order an MRI, which reveals an L5-S1 disc herniation with associated canal stenosis and left neuroforaminal stenosis.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Yang? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.

  "dose": "low",
  "explanation": "I would offer a limited one-week supply of hydrocodone as a bridge to more definitive treatment given the severe pain, while also initiating NSAIDs and arranging surgical consultation."}
